description:
src/ir_interp/backend.rs owns a heap per process, allocates into it, grafts gifts into it and never collects: no path in the interpreter calls Process::collect, so an interpreted process's heap only grows. This is a three-path parity gap; fz-wje (the interpreter charges no reductions, so it never yields) is the sibling gap and is not changed here.

State after fz-gl6.2 (2bffe911c): the JIT and AOT end every quantum with sched_core::end_quantum (collect when due, sweep at exit, drain destructors through Scheduler::run_destructor, return a Disposition). The interpreter loop (drive_backend_until_idle) does not call it: at a Done it calls heap.release_resources_at_exit() and drain_destructors() directly, and at Blocked it only marks the process Blocked. The builder of .2 found that an exit-time collection of an interpreted process would corrupt its heap because the interpreter holds heap values in Rust structures, so it kept the non-collecting exit path.

The interpreter's heap values live outside Process across a boundary:
- BackendRunStep::Done(AnyValue): the return value, read after the boundary into halt_value.
- IrInterpRuntime.backend_resume: HashMap<pid, BackendResumeEntry> (executable args / entry env / continuations) for a process that yields or is woken.
- IrInterpRuntime.backend_parked: HashMap<pid, BackendParkRecord> (env: HashMap<ValueId, BackendBoundValue>, continuations) for a parked receive.
Process::collect roots only the runnable closure, the Process park record, the mailbox and caller transient roots, so none of these is rooted today.

Done when:
- The interpreter's scheduler loop ends every quantum through sched_core::end_quantum, exactly as the JIT and AOT do, and drive_backend_until_idle calls neither release_resources_at_exit nor drain_destructors itself. Every interpreter-held heap value that survives a boundary is a root of that collection and is rewritten to its forwarded value afterwards, through Process::collect's transient roots or by moving the value into a structure Process::collect already roots; choose the one that leaves a single root set, and explain the choice in the commit. No second root assembly.
- Investigate first and record in the commit: every interpreter structure that holds an AnyValue or BackendBoundValue across a boundary, and how each is rooted.
- The fz-gl6.1 pin of zero collections on interp for fixture 00901 moves to a counted value (pinned with an explanation; run and interp are expected to differ while fz-wje keeps the interpreter from yielding), and fixture 00905 (a receiver parked on a pinned list is collected and still matches) pins at least one collection on interp through the gc event.
- A probe program that allocates past the trigger shows gc events on interp, recorded in the commit.
- Fixture 00906's comment says the interpreter does not collect; rewrite it to the new fact. Fixture 00907, 00901 and every other fixture stay green on interp.
- Documentation in the same commit: every .agent/docs page, guide (guides/*.html), README.md section and fixture comment that says the interpreter never collects is rewritten to the present fact, and a grep for "never collects", "does not collect" and "interpreter ... collect" over .agent, guides, README.md and fixtures returns nothing stale. Full gate green (--workspace --all-targets plus doc tests, fixture matrix with --test-threads=1). Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form. No co-author trailer, no attribution line.
title: The interpreter collects at its boundary
